RED, and the test is the repository's own: `cd packages/daemon && LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=... go test ./cmd/legion -run TestClaimsForgetSessionPostsToTheClaimRoute -count=1` fails at this head with `forget-session stdout = "legion-legion-legion-208-architect architect LEGION-208 failed 3 44 - -\n", want "… failed 3 44\n"` (cmd/legion/claims_test.go:571). The same test passes on a detached clone of main at f699b1316430692e5603ecfd1ebc02f12132bb6d, run against the same Postgres, so it is this change's and not the base's.

The cause is this change's two new columns on a claim, the open round and the head its worker reported. `legion claims forget-session` prints the same claims table as `legion claims list`, and the branch updated only the list's assertion — TestClaimsListPrintsOneLinePerClaim, which is the row the pull request body's 'Fails on main' table quotes — leaving the sibling assertion of the same table behind. Either the two columns belong in `forget-session`'s output and the test's want line gains them, or they do not and the printer is wrong; the reader's own consistency says the first.

It escaped because no command of the round ran that package: the implementer's regression command is `go test ./internal/supervise/... ./internal/api/... ./internal/record/... ./internal/runtime/sandbox/...` and `./internal/daemon -run 'PodUpdate|StalePlugin|Plugin'`. CI's `test` job runs the whole module and would have caught it, but CI at this head is still queued (below), so nothing had read it yet.
